images.title: Complete the group of three 7s
images.purpose: Shows the cube root tripler's core move: the primes of 1323 grouped in threes, with one 7 missing, so multiplying by 7 makes a perfect cube.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. The number at the top, two rings of tiles in the middle, and one short result below.
images.exact_structure: At the top centre: 1323 in large dark digits. Below it, two rounded rings side by side. Left ring holds exactly 3 round tiles reading 3, 3, 3, filled teal (#0072B2), complete. Right ring holds exactly 2 round tiles reading 7, 7, filled amber (#E69F00), and one empty dashed vermilion (#D55E00) slot. Below the rings, centred: × 7 gives 21³. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiplying by the missing primes completes every group of three and makes a perfect cube.
